newsitem.title: USA: Hilton, ITT set for hearing.
newsitem.headline: Hilton, ITT set for hearing.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp and ITT Corp on Wednesday were preparing for a hearing in federal court in Las Vegas over Hilton's motion to compel ITT into holding its annual shareholders meeting in May.
The hearing is set to begin at 2:30 p.m. PST (5:30 p.m. EST/2130 GMT) in the courtroom of U.S. District Judge Philip Pro, spokesmen for both companies said.
In January, Hilton launched a $6.5 billion hostile takever bid for ITT, but the $55 per share cash and stock offer was later rejected by ITT as inadequate.

Hilton has nominated a slate of directors to unseat ITT's current board at its next annual meeting, which has traditionally been held in mid-May but could be held as late as mid-November. ITT has yet to schedule the meeting.

In court documents Hilton has asked the Judge Pro to force ITT to hold the meeting in mid-May arguing that ITT's bylaws and Nevada state law require an annual meeting within one year from the previous meeting.

ITT claims its bylaws and state law do not require a mid-May meeting. Indeed, it claims it has 18 months from the previous year's date to hold its annual meeting, which means it could hold the meeting as late as November.
